text:
Honestly i don't think for the average consumer DLSS4 should be considered a selling point.

Unlike DLSS3 this version is rendering 3 fake frames for every 1 real frame. Instead of rendering 1 fake then 1 real back and forth. That is a large amount of time between actual frames. Why this is an issue is that the game will only register your button presses on the real frames.

Meaning that in some genre if games with the largest player bases (shooters, fighters, driving, action adventure) that will require a more accurate timing on your inputs its going to cause u to miss inputs in game. Now the average person may not notice or know exactly what's going on but that's going to be the issue.

Now let's talk about every other genre of game. Well unless your goal is to run every game in 4K ultra wide 100+ frames it's still not a selling point. Why do u need AI frames on farming simulator? Or a RTS my guy?

Im just saying for the average consumer this is more of a gimmick than an actually useful day to day feature.

For content creators and professionals in specific industries this card has alot more potential for certain niche functions.

text:
DLSS and Frame Generator are two different things.

DLSS allows you to play at the same target resolution thanks to AI, by running the game at a lower resolution and then upscaling it. This reduces the load on the GPU’s VRAM and also decreases input lag and latency (since the game operates at a lower resolution, the frames generated are not "fake frames," but the same ones you would get by lowering the resolution manually). For this reason, enabling DLSS is highly recommended in competitive games as well as AAA titles.

The Frame Generator (FG), on the other hand, uses AI to multiply the frames you are playing by generating them "out of thin air." The working resolution remains the same, but this frame generation significantly increases latency. When FG is used in combination with DLSS, compared to rasterized performance, you’ll notice a small increase in latency. However, this might improve in the future with the release of NVIDIA Reflex 2.

The use of FG or the FG + DLSS combo is not recommended for competitive games, but it is highly recommended for AAA titles, as long as the rasterized base performance allows you to hit at least 60 fps. In this way, the increase in latency remains barely noticeable.

​ @dwncasted  The thing you gotta remember is that there's only so much raw computing power you can cram inside something before you can't put in anymore. That's why we haven't been increasing CPU clock speeds that much in the last 10-20 years, and started focusing on adding more cores, better cooling so we can fit more power inside, better temperature resistance so it can fit more heat before overheating (maximum temps used to be like 70C), and being more efficient with the clock speeds and cores we have.

The same thing is going to happen with GPUs. It would be cool if we could have 30% generational improvements forever, but this won't happen.
